Collided

Lauren Asher, Maria Adam (Translator)

3.78

Rate this book
O poveste captivantă romance despre rivalitate, atracție și secrete periculoase de la autoarea seriilor-bestseller „Miliardarii de la Dreamland” și „Miliardarii de pe malul lacului”.

SOPHIE

Liam este băiatul de aur al Formulei 1. Dar, în realitate, nu e decât un escroc.

Fermecător. Diabolic. Seducător.

În plus, mi-a promis că o să mă ajute să-mi transform în realitate toate dorințele obraznice pe care mi le-am imaginat.

Îl împing în zona sigură a prieteniei.

Însă, în loc să accepte această relație de amiciție, el face un pariu.

Un sezon. O listă. Un secret murdar.


LIAM

Sophie este ca și cum cea mai mare fantezie a mea a prins viață.

Totuși, ea reprezintă o amenințare pentru reînnoirea contractului meu.

Face parte din echipa rivală, așa că eu ar trebui să nu cedez.

Toată lumea se împotrivește prieteniei dintre noi.

Șeful meu. Tatăl ei. Eu.

Și totuși, sunt captivat de ea și de Lista Dorințelor Obraznice pe care a întocmit-o.

La naiba cu iubirea platonică! Eu vreau una catastrofală!

Una din acele cărți de dragoste cu care te identifici și care dă dependență.

About Me:

Lauren Asher is a New York Times, USA Today, Sunday Times, Globe and Mail, and Publishers Weekly bestselling author of contemporary romance. She enjoys writing about flawed yet relatable characters you can’t help falling in love with and fictional worlds you wish were real.

Her favorite activities outside of writing include DIY projects, binging old episodes of Parks and Rec, and searching Yelp for new restaurants before choosing her trusted favorite. She works best after her morning coffee and will never deny a nap.

“What’s your favorite book? Doubt colors my voice.
"If you have a favorite, I don’t trust you. Any book lover has at least five they can name off the top of their head.”

I honestly enjoyed this book a lot but it was very slow for my liking and kind of did get me into a minor slump if I am being honest. Lauren's writing here was spectacular, so easy to read and entertaining and the way she focused on the romance more through the first 70% and then switched to f1 was really well done. I appreciate that she actually took time to do some research about it because otherwise I honestly would have rioted.

The characters Liam and Sophie were an absolute joy to read because Liam is a Brandon Sanderson fan, flirty, cocky and so much fun to be around. I honestly found myself liking his chapters a lot. The dialogues and his humor was really fun to read and Sophie was witty and charismatic too, although I was annoyed by her at times, her reactions were justified so I was okay with her.

The romance was so hot and sizzling! I mean- of course it would be as there was a naughty bucket list involved. Though I really enjoyed the bucket list scenes and for a thing that was actually a main part of the book...I found it loosing its charm as we went through the book but that does not negate how well written there relationship was and how much I enjoyed their chemistry and their banter. Truth be told I was anticipating their book as soon as I met them.

All in all, I really enjoyed it! it was spicy and fun to read but the only issue I had was the pacing which made me drop it to a three and I am pretty sure because of that I wont reread it ever.

Ended up having a better time than I expected. A F1 romance with good girl x bad boy vibes and friends to lovers is something one will surely enjoy. Pair it with juicy spice and you got yourself the full package 👀

The prologue was so awesome. The beginning dull but the middle was EVERYTHING I wanted- flirting, banter, cutesy moments, and a good plot. The ending was kind of rushed imo as the third act drama deserved to be resolved properly. The man went from being confused to proposing within a few pages and that didn't sit well with me- why was why it wasn't a perfect read for me. The "naughty list" was a storyline I had a lot of fun with.

Liam and Sophie had such explosive chemistry. I loved reading their adorable moments, their sexy moments and their story which had a fair bit of drama towards the end. Guys when I tell you, Lauren Asher can write good smut, believe you me 🤌

Before reading, I was fully expecting Liam to frustrate me. It didn't happen and boy, am I glad. Liam won me over. There was a lot of depth to him, despite his cocky side. Also, the mouth on that man 🥵🫦 *fans self* I loved getting to know him. I liked that he read books and always made Sophie comfortable, helped her with the naughty list.

Sophie was adorable. I liked that she had a kinky side to her underneath her innocent demeanour. While she was good, I believe she got overshadowed by Liam and his storyline. I know it's a F1 romance and the focus will be a tad more on the racer, but she didn't really have much happening with her except romancing the guy.

Anyway, I still have no opinions on Jax. Hopefully his book will live up too.

3.5 ☆


“My beautiful angel. Too wicked for heaven, too good for hell.” I may be his beautiful angel, but he’s my masked devil— too naughty for my heart, too irresistible for my body."


This was cute, and I enjoyed it more than 'Throttled.' There were fewer cringe and cheesy moments, and the writing overall improved. If you like racing and enjoy a good bucket list, then you will enjoy this.


Collided is the second book in the Dirty Air series and is a friends to friends with benefits to lovers, bad boy/good girl, F1 racing romance that was filled with witty banter, lust and sexual tension Aside from the moment in the first chapter that had my heart breaking and left me crying, this had me literally smiling and laughing out loud.


Sophie Mitchell is the daughter of one of F1s principles and is attending university. One night after having another bad hookup that left her unsatisfied and wanting more she decides that she needs more fun in her life while drinking a bottle of wine, she comes up with a 'Fuck It' list consisting of adventures and naughty things. Now, she just needs to convince her dad to allow her to come visit for the season. He obliges as long as she agrees to his set of rules. The number one rule is to stay away from the racers. The first gala she attends of the season she is met by none other than Liam Zander a driver for McCoy, her dads rival team and Sophie is no longer the girl he met three years ago at a princess party piquing his interest. Liam discovers her list and offers to help her check the items off, he even adds go on a date with a bad boy after he wins a bet they made, except Sophie wants to just be friends and he reluctantly agrees. They both pushed and pulled against the line of their friendship for many months, teetering on the edge of it. But will she give in to their chemistry and let him know her feelings for him? And will he be able to set aside his fears of love and give her what she craves with him?


Seeing more of Maya and Noah was truly a highlight. I loved the friendship that Sophie and Maya built and especially loved when Noah was giving Liam relationship advice (talk about swooning). We don't see too much of Jax, but he pulled at my heartstrings when he offered up some advice to Liam.


“But remember this. I want to get to know all of you, including the parts you’re too scared to share. I want to learn about the man no one else knows. So give me every part of you because I’m not here to piece you back together. I like you too much, just the way you are, broken parts and all.”

"The girl whose eyes twinkle as bright as the very things she loves to watch. And while you were busy staring up at the vast nothingness, I’d watch you while envying a damn sky. A sky for fuck’s sake. But at the time, I didn’t realize I wanted you to look at me that way. With unconditional love.”


Liam and Sophie had a chemistry that was unquestionable. I absolutely loved their friendship and watching it bud into something more. I adored the dates that Liam planned for her while helping her check off her list (my favorites were that he took her skydiving and to see the stars). The one thing that annoyed me most was how Sophie would rather be miserable and make her dad happy rather than doing what makes her happy. Liam helped her with that by encouraging her to chase and persue her dreams while Sophie was the person who could get Liam to open up about his fears helping him to overcome them and to understand that its okay to grieve.


I could have done without the third act breakup as it was unnecessary and could have been prevented if they had just communicated about the deal that was looming overhead and how they were each feeling. I fell in love with the epilogue because it was the sweetest and had me feeling butterflies and swooning with them. I enjoyed this and am excited to find out what's to come with Jax next.

and the series continues to be a dud.

Truthfully, it's just disappointing because as I stated in my Throttled review, this series has a lot of hype and really only good things being said about it. If F1 racers are really like this in the three-dimensional world and not just in this fictional one—count me out.

Liam and Sophie to me had more of a connection than Maya and Noah. Their story also felt a little more intimate and emotional compared to the predecessor book, yet it still made my skin crawl and didn't give enough. Liam's inner dialogue was truly disturbing. This was one of the same points I made in the last book. Always about sex and I am all for one for smutty reads. GIVE THEM TO ME. This just was all portrayed and delivered very gag-worthy.

Now, one of my biggest problems which also goes towards Throttled is the trauma angle. The author gave Liam a traumatic experience that hindered him and created some of his bad characteristics and so on. Yet... for such a big point they made around it, it truly wasn't touched on very much or discussed nearly enough to make it seem important to the story to me. Traumatic stuff, if being added to a book, shouldn't take a back seat. It's like it was added for shits and giggles just because it was completely disregarded for almost the entirety of the book. Just doesn't sit well with me.

Sophie is a uni student who never had any orgasms in her life and she shackled her life to an idea of making her dad feel proud so she never did anything for herself until one night at 2 am she wrote a 'Fuck it' list filled with some adventures and a few naughty things she wanted to do. “I hope your ego can handle a blow here and there because I plan on winning.” I gaze into Liam’s eyes.
“There are few things I like blown, and that’s not one of them.” Liam grins


“And your plan somehow includes a replica of your cock?” My eyes bulge. He winks.
“As much as I love hearing that word from your mouth, behave for our guests.”



So basically the whole story was based on a bucket list and I was invested in the story from the very first page. I didn't loved the story or the characters but this book was enjoyable nonetheless. I enjoyed the 60% of the book so much because Sophie and Liam were friends and all the tension and lust made everything hot and all but the moment they give in to this sexual tension between them and became friends with benefits I kinda lost my interest in the story. I was enjoying it but not the way I loved their friendship.


"His lips tug into a smile before they brush up against my temple, giving me the faintest kiss. One so soft, I almost think I made it up."


"Liking Sophie is kind of like jumping out of a plane. Exhilarating, addicting, and damn near impossible to forget."



The writing has improved in this one and it was less cringe and had vivid characters. The spice was hot and I can always count on Lauren for hot and delicious scenes ❤️‍🔥🤌🏻 But for me this book was so long considering it could be 50 to 80 pages less if all the unnecessary drama in the end didn't happen.


➺ Liam Zander
A Handsome, charming and a funny boy who loves reading books and uses chess refrences. He reads book every night and loves classics 🤭💘 he is such a hot nerdy F1 boi. Liam says he can't fall in love with because he is afraid of what happened to his brother's love. I loved him from the first moment and yes he is a manwhore and all but when Sophie came in picture he never laid his eyes on anyone but 'only her'. His inability to see that he is made for love frustrated me so much and I know he had his reasons but he was downright ignoring what he felt for Sophie and it took five persons to make him realise he is in love with his best friend.

“Ready to fly, Sunshine?” It’s not my fault she looks and acts like the sun. Like the destructive yellow orb in the sky, she eats away at my protective layer while lighting up my darkest corners.


➺ Sophie Mitchell
A blond girl with her enormous love for graphic tees and sneakers. She is ambitious, funny and kind and loves to organise and plan for things in advance thats why that list. I liked her and she is so much mature considering her age and understands Liam and his painful past and thats what I liked about her the most. But I hated how she never made her own decisions in her life when she clearly wasn't liking what her father made her study for. I loved how she helped Liam to get over his past and to sought out his feelings and grief.

"Like Liam can sense my doubts, he tugs on my hair and draws me back into the moment. He erases my concerns with his lips. This man kisses me like it may be our last, branding himself, so I never forget him. And God, I’ll never."



➙ Liam and Sophie's realtionship

Their realtionship started as friends to friends with benefits to lovers. It was quite an interesting transition but I liked their relationship progress. It was real and they both needed well more like Liam needed time to accept his fears about Love and everything. For months they were tip toeing around each other, playing mind games and all because Sophie was scared to give in to this attraction between them and Liam never wanted to involve any feelings between their friendship.


"I want to learn every inch of you while I map out your body like the night sky you love so damn much."


"Kissing Sophie makes me question what the fuck I’ve been doing before. Scratch that— kissing Sophie feels like everything."



They both had undeniable chemistry, sparks and the tension between them was so hot and palpable ❤️‍🔥 half the time I just wanted them to give in to this lust just so they can stop this torture. I loved their friendship so much, their witty bantering and teasing, their cute little dates and how they both helped each other. I loved how he took Sophie to see the stars and took her to skydiving and many other dates. It was definitely one of the best moments of liamsophie. Liam helped Sophie to pursue her dreams and Sophie helped him to understand that its okay to grieve and have your fears until they eat you up alive. Liam needed someone who can helped him understand the meaning of love and family. Sophie was his person.


“But remember this. I want to get to know all of you, including the parts you’re too scared to share. I want to learn about the man no one else knows. So give me every part of you because I’m not here to piece you back together. I like you too much, just the way you are, broken parts and all.”


“The girl whose eyes twinkle as bright as the very things she loves to watch. And while you were busy staring up at the vast nothingness, I’d watch you while envying a damn sky. A sky for fuck’s sake. But at the time, I didn’t realize I wanted you to look at me that way. With unconditional love.”



The ending was sweet and wholesome though I hated the third act breakup and it wasn't needed if Sophie just talked with Liam about that deal and cleared all their misunderstandings. I loved the epilogue it was so cute and everything and considering I don't really love HEA so it was perfect. All in all it was an amazing read and definitely worth a read if you are in a mood for a F1 book with a friends to lovers trope.
